title: Priest Lake Museum

services.name: History of Luby Bay Cabin
services.desc: The Luby Bay Ranger Station log cabin is one of the most visible legacies of the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) at Priest Lake. The United States Forest Service designed this rustic cabin and oversaw its construction in 1934 and 1935. Two truckloads of young men from the Kalispell Bay CCC camp came each day to work on the cabin under the tutelage of local men like Fulton Messmore. Messmore instructed the CCC boys how to cut and notch the western larch logs, then plane and varnish them. He taught them to split cedar shakes for the roof and to turn gathered rocks into a remarkable fireplace. services.name: Museum Exhibits
services.desc: History is all around us, so the museum created outdoor exhibit panels you can visit anytime! The Kalispel Language Survival School with J.R. Bluff worked with the museum to create this outdoor interpretative panel about the Tribe’s long connection to Priest Lake. A panel is located along the beach at the museum and another one is on the east side of the lake at Soldier Creek, where Sherwood Beach roads end. Listen to J.R. Bluff read the panel in Salish and English. Priest Lake Museum is a volunteer-run 501c3 non-profit organization dedicated to collecting and sharing the cultural and natural history of the region. blurb: The Priest Lake Museum is free to visitors and shares the story of how Priest Lake is shaped by its people, its landscapes, and the generations who have called this remarkable place home. We share the area’s cultural and natural history through engaging exhibits, historic photographs, treasured artifacts, and community stories.
